# REAMIMA

> Engineering and R&D company (Ingeniería, I+D+i) based in Spain. One that treats complexity as an advantage, not an obstacle. One of the few that know when the hard way is better even when the easy way exists.

REAMIMA TECH, S.L.U. designs and builds what conventional engineering considers out of reach. Capabilities span the full stack: hardware, electronics, full industrial automation (sensor, network, PLC/Simatic, SCADA, MES), real-time control, high-performance software and product design. On-device processing — no servers, no cloud, privacy as system architecture. Open hardware when it matters (OSHWA certified). What seems impossible to run — simply works.

# About REAMIMA · Engineering and R&D. Automation experts.  —  https://www.reamima.com/sobre

REAMIMA: engineering and R&D team. Technical capabilities, principles and projects.

About REAMIMA

## An engineering company that designs what does not yet exist.

REAMIMA is an engineering and R&D team focused on solving problems the industry considers out of reach. Hardware, electronics, real-time control and high-performance software.

Mission

To build what conventional engineering discarded as unviable. To make the complex simple. To return technical control to the user.

We operate at the frontier where low-cost electronics, embedded processing and rigorous design converge into systems that seem impossible — and simply work.

Engineering principles

01 / Rigor

### The hard part, first

We start with the toughest technical constraint. If it doesn’t hold there, it doesn’t hold anywhere.

02 / Soberanía

### Edge processing

Data is processed where it is generated. No intermediate servers. Privacy is a system property, not a promise.

03 / Apertura

### Open hardware when it matters

When a system can save lives, its design is published. OSHWA certification is the documentary proof, not a decorative badge.

04 / Síntesis

### Complexity lives inside

The user never sees the difficulty. What reaches their hand is clear, calm and useful.

Technical capabilities

### Hardware and electronics

Rapid prototype design on Arduino, ESP32, M5Stack, Portenta, Raspberry and industrial PLCs (Simatic, Logo, IOT2020). Sensor integration, relay control, low-cost electronics with industrial tolerance.

### Embedded and mobile software

Real-time signal processing, on-device algorithms, server-less architectures. Mobile applications that live on the phone and respect privacy by construction.

### Systems design

Most people design parts. We design systems. A holistic vision isn't improvised — it's built through years of real projects.

### For top-tier projects

Some projects require more than engineering — they require an ecosystem. We work with top-tier industrial partners to scale when the project demands it, so the client doesn't have to look for them.

Current projects

### Cardistream

Physical performance optimization software that builds each person’s unique training pattern over time. On-device processing. Zero servers.

[cardistream.com](https://cardistream.com)

### iSoStream

A new training metric inside Cardistream. The number that synthesises your training digital twin — what no coach can calculate by eye.

# Open-hardware emergency ventilator (2020) · REAMIMA  —  https://www.reamima.com/origenes

2020: REAMIMA designs an emergency ventilator from off-the-shelf materials. Hardware certified by OSHWA

Marzo · 2020

## When the world stopped, we didn’t.

REAMIMA was born in the first weeks of lockdown, designing an emergency ventilator from materials anyone could order from home: off-the-shelf pumps from any hardware store, an Arduino board and a few sensors. Open, free, replicable hardware.

March 2020 · engineer in laboratory developing the first prototype

The project

Building a ventilator from off-the-shelf materials.

REAMIMA is the open and free hardware design so that anyone can help by building ventilators with easily available materials, without needing a compressed-air line.

The first prototype was assembled with empty bottles, a plastic container, two standard water pumps, the kind found in any hardware store, and electronics that anyone could buy on Amazon or at electronics stores. The idea was to walk into a hardware store and find everything needed to build a ventilator. In simple words: the ventilator McGyver would build.

The design is based on the use of water columns to produce gas exchange in the lung in a simple way. In an emergency, as we faced with the Coronavirus, it was necessary to build reliable-enough equipment quickly, without developing new material that would need many hours of validation.

Most importantly: with very little knowledge anyone could assemble a small ventilator. That was — and remains — REAMIMA’s wager: serious engineering that reaches the hands of whoever needs it.

The principle

### A water pump between two tanks.

The whole system fits in one idea: a pump moves water between a compression tank and a main tank. The water column rising in the first compresses the air inside an inverted bottle and sends it to the patient. When the water falls, the bottle refills with air.

International recognition

### Verified, published and shared with the global community.

Technical demonstration

### The system, in operation.

Technical documentation

### Three models. From air to control.

#### Air treatment

Humidification, heating and cleaning. Preparing the air the patient breathes.

Read documentation

#### Simple Model

Two containers, two pumps, timer control. The essence of the system, step by step, with calculations.

Read documentation

#### Advanced Model

Pressure control, assisted expiration, safety valves and monitoring. The evolution of the simple model.

Read documentation

The natural way

A crisis does not create capabilities. It reveals them. The cool head under pressure. The collaboration nobody called for. Do engineering without manufacturing or ordering parts — with what you have on the shelf.

That is what we do: engineering that does not wait for perfect conditions, but makes real conditions exactly enough.

# Simple Model · Origins · REAMIMA  —  https://www.reamima.com/origenes-simple

Simple Model of the REAMIMA ventilator: tanks, pumps and timers. Technical documentation with calculations and diagrams.

[Origins](https://www.reamima.com/origenes) · 02 · Simple

## Simple Model

A large container that acts as a water reservoir and a smaller one called the inspiration tank. The essence of the system, step by step, with calculations.

Main components

### Pumps, relays and a timer. Nothing else.

Submersible water pump

Two units. One moves water to the inspiration tank; the other returns it.

Power relays

Switch each pump’s 220 V supply based on timer commands.

Standard heater

Same as in the air subsystem: keeps the water at temperature.

The simplest model to build a ventilator is a large container that acts as a water reservoir and a smaller one we call the inspiration tank. At the output of the bottle that compresses the air (in the video, where the glove is mounted), the ventilator tube connects to a mask with a valve, so that exhalation occurs naturally.

In the video, the materials used are visible: an empty milk bottle as inspiration tank, an empty soap bottle as inspiration container, and a transparent plastic box as system water tank. Inside the milk bottle there is a standard water pump; inside the system water tank, another pump. Both pumps are connected to two relays controlled by a timer.

01 · Botella

### The air-compressing bottle

Volume above 700–1,000 ml; 1,200 ml is recommended. It can be a bottle, a tube of methacrylate, PVC or metal — rigid, easy to obtain and with a mouth on top to connect the ventilator tube.

The inverted bottle must be firmly attached to the tank, not moving, and must not leak air when screwed to the wall of the inspiration tank. If you pierce it for fixing, seal with an inert material (silicone) or with non-porous clear tape. The pressure is not high and tape holds.

Position: in the inspiration vessel, with the pump at the bottom, leave two or three fingers of water above the pump and a couple up to the base of the bottle. That space fills with air during expiration and is covered during inspiration.

02 · Cotas

### Levels 0, 1 and 2

**Level 0** — minimum water level of the tank (you can mark it). **Level 1** — water starts to cover the base of the air-compressing bottle. From here on, the air volume starts to flow through the tube. **Level 2** — mark inside the bottle, roughly 500 ml from its base. This is the level the water must reach inside the bottle to guarantee that 500 ml of air is delivered to the outside.

In the video example, with a 800 ml bottle, the base was removed, the bottle placed upside down with the cap on, filled with water and decanted into a 500-ml-marked container. You can add more graduations (600 ml, 400 ml, etc.) in case more or less air needs to be insufflated.

03 · Bombas

### Flow calculation

Both pumps are standard water pumps, the kind sold in any hardware store. The flow must be enough to fill 1 litre inside the compression bottle, and it depends on the inspiration tank volume.

Measure or calculate the height between level 0 and level 2 inside the inspiration bottle. Multiplied by the area of the inspiration tank, you get the cm³ the pump must move.

Ventilators work between 10 and 30 breaths per minute. We must fill those 4.5 L 30 times per minute. Since each cycle inhales and exhales, the rate doubles: 30 × 2 = 60.

A single pump for this flow is expensive and uncommon; look for the highest available flow (most have a regulator to lower it). A real option is the Waldbeck Nemesis T90: 90 W, up to 4 m head, IPX8, 6,200 L/h.

With that pump 10–12 breaths per minute are reached comfortably, or several pumps can be used to raise frequency. Always check that the chosen pump physically fits inside the inspiration tank.

04 · Relés

### Safe switching

In this case the pumps run at 220 V. Of the two plug wires, one goes to the relay and the other to one of the poles. The other relay terminal (AC side) connects to the other pole, closing the circuit. **⚠ Caution: this is AC — handle with care.**

To withstand frequent on/off cycles, a solid-state relay is recommended — for instance, DC-AC 5 V/2 A 4-channel modules with fuse. They handle a 440 W load per pump without issue.

05 · Control

### Whatever you have at hand

Use the device you prefer: a maker can use Arduino, ESP32, M5Stack; with PLC experience, a Simatic, Logo or IOT2020; if you program and you like Raspberry, that works too. What matters is that the operator of the ventilator will speak in clinical terms, foreign to your programming: design a human-machine interface that lets them easily set breath time and/or air volume.

A personal note: my apologies to David Cuartielles and Massimo Banzi for using an M5Stack in the video instead of a Portenta H7 or another original Arduino board. I needed it fast, with a screen, and I knew its dual core well enough for simultaneous programming. Without their work on Arduino this would not have been possible. What David and Massimo set in motion two decades ago was a bet that anyone with an idea and a real problem could build the solution. In the spring of 2020, millions of makers proved them right. Thanks to them, their team and that whole community.

06 · Tiempos

### Program: three timers, two outputs

The program is very simple: three timers activate two digital outputs.

**D** is the total cycle time in seconds (60/D = breaths per minute). **A** is the time in seconds during which the chosen volume is insufflated. **B** is the pause (optional, decided by the ventilation expert) and **C** is the expiration time, during which the second pump is activated to return water to the tank.

To fill from level 0 to level 2 in the given time, generate a PWM pulse train during time A. A couple of tests will be needed to find the right setting.

One more thing: keep a power strip with a switch and a mop nearby. The first is to stop everything at once. The second, for when you don't get there in time. We know this from experience.

# Advanced Model · Origins · REAMIMA  —  https://www.reamima.com/origenes-avanzado

Evolution of the Simple Model: pressure control, assisted expiration, sensors and clinical monitoring of the REAMIMA ventilator.

[Origins](https://www.reamima.com/origenes) · 03 · Advanced

## Advanced Model

The evolution of the Simple Model. Pressure control, assisted expiration, in-line sensors and clinical monitoring. The same idea, taken to the next level of safety.

The Advanced Model keeps the water column and the inverted bottle of the Simple Model — that idea remains the heart of the system — and adds what separates emergency equipment from clinically safe equipment: pressure control, in-line sensors, assisted expiration, redundant safety valves and real-time monitoring.

We built the prototypes needed to prove it worked. When the pandemic stabilised, there was no reason to continue — and that is exactly what we wanted: for it not to be needed. This page documents the complete design.

01 · Pressure

### Inspiratory pressure control

A differential sensor measures inspiratory line pressure in real time. The controller modulates pump flow via PWM to keep pressure within the clinical window set by the operator. If the threshold is exceeded, the safety valve relieves immediately.

For measurement we evaluated Bosch Sensortec's environmental sensor family: [BME280](https://www.bosch-sensortec.com/products/environmental-sensors/humidity-sensors-bme280/), [BME680](https://www.bosch-sensortec.com/products/environmental-sensors/gas-sensors/bme680/), [BME690](https://www.bosch-sensortec.com/products/environmental-sensors/gas-sensors/bme690/) and [BME688](https://www.bosch-sensortec.com/products/environmental-sensors/gas-sensors/bme688/). They combine barometric pressure, temperature and humidity in a compact package, with sufficient accuracy for emergency ventilation and reasonable availability during the 2020 supply crisis.

PIP

Peak inspiratory pressure

Adjustable limit, audible and visual alarm.

PEEP

Positive end-expiratory pressure

Maintained by the return water column and a calibrated valve.

02 · Flow

### Measured flow and tidal volume

A flow sensor on the inspiratory branch — Venturi-effect or thermal anemometer, depending on availability — allows the flow to be integrated over time and yields the actual tidal volume delivered per cycle. That closes the volume loop and frees the operator from estimating it from the levels.

03 · Expiration

### Assisted expiration and PEEP valve

In the Simple Model, expiration is passive. In the Advanced Model, the expiratory branch passes through a calibrated valve that maintains PEEP and through a second water column that acts as a one-way seal. An auxiliary pump assists expiration when clinically required.

04 · Monitor

### Clinical interface and telemetry

A screen with real-time pressure, flow and volume waveforms, editable parameters (rate, tidal volume, PEEP, PIP, FiO₂) and alarms. Data is logged locally and, optionally, sent to a hospital monitoring system.

05 · Safety

### Redundancy and safe modes

Dual relief valve, redundant pressure sensor, firmware watchdog, integrated UPS power and a manual mode independent of the controller. If the digital system fails, the water column keeps running: that was, from the beginning, one of the design principles.

For more demanding environments — intensive care units with zero tolerance for interruption — the natural step up is controller-level redundancy. The [Siemens Simatic S7-1500 H](https://www.siemens.com/es-es/products/simatic/s7-1500-rh-cpus/) is the industrial reference: two hot-synchronised CPUs that switch without state loss if one fails. An architecture designed exactly for this.

R&D line paused in 2021. The documentation is kept here as technical and historical reference.

---

# Air treatment · Origins · REAMIMA  —  https://www.reamima.com/origenes-tratamiento-aire

Humidification, heating and cleaning of the air. Technical documentation of the air-preparation subsystem of the REAMIMA ventilator.

[Origins](https://www.reamima.com/origenes) · 01 · Air

## Air treatment

The air a patient breathes, in an emergency, may enter untreated — as in the manual ventilators we see in films. But with very little more it can be properly prepared: humidified, at the right temperature and free of pathogens.

Components

### Three standard parts you can buy at any shop.

Standard air pump

+20,000 hours of service. Releases air inside the warm water.

Standard heater

Low failure rate, temperature range suited to the subsystem.

UV lamp

Sterilises the air chamber. Shielded, never visible directly.

01 · Humectación

### Heat and humidify

The air must be heated to the right temperature and given the humidity it needs. A standard air pump — tested at over 20,000 hours of operation (check the manufacturer’s data sheet) — releases the air into a water tank at controlled temperature.

02 · Calentamiento

### Standard heating element

To heat the air, we again use a standard part. Heaters of this type have many years of field experience, a low failure rate, easy availability and a temperature range similar to what the subsystem needs.

03 · Construcción

### Tank and sizing

The simplest approach is to use a plastic or metal container as the water tank for the whole circuit. The size must accommodate the air of several breaths.

#### Required air volume

If we take a maximum of 10 ml/kg of air and the ventilator is designed for 100 kg, that is 1,000 ml of air per inspiration. The air tank must exceed this volume multiplied by 2 (breaths) and by 3 (air + water + others), so a 6-litre tank is the recommended starting point.

#### Required airflow

We must plan for 15 to 25 breaths per minute. In the worst case (1,000 ml × 25 br/min) we obtain 25,000 litres/hour. With this figure we size the air pump that will treat the air to be breathed.

The pump must release the air into the hot water, as shown in the diagram, producing a bubble flow that is humidified and heated before reaching the inspiration circuit.

04 · Limpieza

### UV sterilisation

The water must be replaced and the system cleaned regularly to prevent the proliferation of bacteria, fungi and other harmful elements. A good solution is to place a standard UV lamp in the tank — also on sale at any shop — designed to eliminate bacteria and keep the water clean.

**Important:** the lamp must be protected and not directly visible. Ultraviolet light can cause serious damage — burns, blindness. Always follow the manufacturer’s instructions.

05 · Seguridad

### Valve and levels

The safety valve is necessary to prevent overpressure or depression conditions that would stop the system from working. The tank should be marked with maximum and minimum water levels, so the volume is always kept within the working range.

06 · Redundancia

### Standby duplicate elements

During the pandemic, the scarcity of materials prevented duplicating the system's elements. Under normal conditions, the right approach is to install each critical component twice: one active and one in standby, ready to take over if the first one fails.

This scheme can be programmed so that the switchover is automatic and imperceptible, similar to the high-availability architecture of Siemens [Simatic H](https://www.siemens.com/es-es/products/simatic/s7-1500-rh-cpus/) PLCs: if one module fails, the system continues operating without interruption while the faulty element is replaced.

# Accessibility · REAMIMA  —  https://www.reamima.com/accesibilidad

REAMIMA's commitment to web accessibility and a channel for reporting access barriers.

Accessibility

## We want no one left out

We work to make this site usable by anyone, with any device or assistive technology. If you find something that does not work well for you, we want to know.

### Our approach

We use the **Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1, level AA** as our reference. We are not a public body and are not legally required to comply, but we believe it is the right thing to do.

This site is static, maintained by a small team. We do what is within our reach within those constraints. When someone points out a barrier, we take note and consider it in subsequent reviews.

### Measures taken

Among the things we have incorporated or reviewed:

- «Skip to content» link visible when using the keyboard, on all pages.
- Semantic structure with `<main>`, `<nav>`, `<footer>` and heading hierarchy.
- Colour contrast reviewed: text on light backgrounds ≥ 4.5:1 (WCAG AA).
- `alt` attributes on all images — descriptive on informational images, empty on decorative ones.
- Navigation menu operable with keyboard; focus moves to the first link when opening the mobile menu.
- Drop-down language selector with 11 languages, operable with keyboard.

WCAG 2.1 Nivel AA Reviewed May 2026

### Report a barrier

If you have found something that prevents or hinders you from using this site, tell us. We do not promise to resolve every case or by when, but we do read it, consider it, and take it into account when we review the site.

### 9. Applicable law and jurisdiction

This Legal Notice is governed by Spanish law. For the resolution of any dispute arising from access to or use of the Website, the parties submit to the courts established under applicable procedural rules and, unless the Law provides otherwise, to those of the registered office of REAMIMA TECH, S.L.U.
